observations.content: User supplied nine context-only preparation packets containing historical requirements and repository excerpts for an observational-memory implementation, explicitly instructing the assistant not to implement during preparation.

Historical requirements to preserve for a later implementation: observer and consolidator worker runs expose actual pi usage costs to the parent, including ephemeral or unsuccessful runs when valid usage exists; valid costs persist in the session ledger with role/run identity; totals include every branch, including abandoned branches; missing, malformed, non-finite, or negative costs must not corrupt totals; totals appear in status/footer UI; focused tests cover aggregation, invalid entries, handoff, and display.

The supplied observational-memory plan specifies Phase A short-term memory followed by Phase B long-term memory, bespoke child_process spawning of ordinary recorded pi worker sessions, vendored minimal ledger modules, a shared worker extension selected by OM_WORKER, orchestrator-assigned timestamp IDs, strong default Claude Sonnet 4.6 models, and a default-OFF per-session /om gate.

The supplied implementation excerpts describe an orchestrator that runs parallel observers over fixed token-bounded conversation slices, commits observations to branch-local ledger entries, and renders deterministic compaction memory with chunk-boundary cutoffs and observer-wait fast paths.

The supplied Phase B design promotes oldest active observations into durable project .memory topic files and JOURNEY.md via one scoped consolidator worker at a time, updates orchestrator-owned INDEX.md, and tombstones the handed batch intersected with still-active observations; long-term files do not roll back under /tree.

The supplied README reports Phase A and Phase B as implemented, with commands /om, /om on/off, /om:status, /om:compact, and /om:consolidate; configuration includes chunk, pool, compaction, journey, concurrency, model, passive, and debug-log settings.

The supplied worker design makes observer prompts recorded pi -p user messages and writes observations through record_observations IPC; consolidator tools read/write/edit/ls/grep only within .memory and prohibit INDEX.md edits.

The supplied source and tests cover timestamp assignment and collision suffixes, branch-ledger folding and tombstones, token clocks and source chunking, compaction projection/cutoffs, memory paths and rendering, pool promotion, subprocess IPC, TUI gauges/workers, and timeline rendering; no test execution result was provided.
